question: Which layer of the adrenal cortex is responsible for secreting aldosterone?
Excessive growth hormone release in adults leads to which condition?
Strychnine is known to hyper-stimulate the motor nervous system in the anterior horn cells of the spinal cord. What is the mechanism of action of strychnine?

answers.option: Blocks glycine uptake at neuromuscular junction

question: A 23-year-old woman has a routine health status examination. Her body mass index is 22. Laboratory studies show fasting plasma glucose is 120 mg/dL. Urinalysis shows mild glucosuria, but no ketonuria or proteinuria. She has no detectable insulin autoantibodies. Her father was similarly affected at age 20. She is most likely to have a mutation in a gene encoding for which of the following?

An 8-year-old child presents to the outpatient department for short height. His height is 106 cm, and his weight is 16 kg. He was normal at birth. He looks chubby and immature but with a normal IQ. Growth velocity is decreased. X-ray shows delayed bone age at 3 years. The most likely cause of short stature in this child would be which of the following?

A 44-year-old man sees his physician because of a ''lump'' on the left side of his neck. Physical examination shows a non-tender nodule on the left lobe of the thyroid gland. A cervical node is also enlarged and non-tender. Laboratory studies show no thyroid autoantibodies in his serum, and the T4 and TSH levels are normal. A thyroidectomy is performed. High-power microscopic examination of the thyroid shows Orphan Annie eye nuclei, nuclear grooves, and psammoma bodies. Which of the following is most likely to contribute to the development of the thyroid nodule in this patient?

A 73-year-old woman has noticed a 10-kg weight loss in the past 3 months. She is becoming increasingly icteric and has constant vague epigastric pain, nausea, and episodes of bloating and diarrhea. There is mild tenderness to palpation in the upper abdomen, but bowel sounds are present. Her stool is negative for occult blood. Laboratory findings include a total serum bilirubin concentration of 11.6 mg/dL and a direct bilirubin level of 10.5 mg/dL. Which of the following conditions involving the pancreas is most likely to be present?
A medical student is preparing an abstract for a case report. The most critical element to include in the abstract is:

answers.option: Introduction and relevance of the case

question: A student copies text from a journal article and pastes it into his assignment without citation. The term that best describes this act is:
A research article contains an abstract with these sections: introduction, Methods, Results, and Conclusion. The Type of abstract described here is?

1 month old baby has been vomiting persistently since birth. On examination he is dehydrated and genitalia are normal. Lab reports show decreased Na, Increased K, RBS 40 mg/dl, pH 7.3, HCO3 10. Most likely cause?
Which of the following should be included in the discussion section?

answers.option: Contrasting result of your study with other studies

question: A 7-year-old boy comes for his annual check-up. His weight is 28 kg and his height is 120 cm, yielding a BMI of approximately 19.4 kg/m³. His BMI places him at a high percentile for his age and sex. His linear growth is consistent with his familial potential, and there are no red flags suggestive of endocrine or genetic syndromes. His diet and physical activity are typical for his peers, and there are no concerning comorbidities noted. What is the most correct interpretation of his nutritional status?

A 9-year-old girl is brought to the pediatric clinic by her mother due to concerns about progressive weight gain over the last two years. On examination, her BMI is above the 97th percentile for her age and sex. Her height is appropriate for her age, and pubertal signs are consistent with her age (Tanner Stage II). The child spends most of her day indoors, watches TV for 4-5 hours daily, and does not participate in any physical activity. She has a strong preference for sugary drinks and fast foods. Her father has type 2 diabetes, and her mother had gestational diabetes during pregnancy. Her birth weight was 4.2 kg. Which of the following is the most significant modifiable risk factor contributing to this child's obesity?

A child has gained excessive weight over the past 1.5 years. His height is normal for his age, and there are no signs of endocrinological disorders. His diet includes frequent intake of fried snacks, sugary beverages, and large portion sizes. He skips breakfast 4-5 days a week and eats while watching screens. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial dietary advice to help this child manage his obesity?

answers.option: Start a strict calorie-restricted ketogenic diet
Switch to meal replacement shakes and supplements
Advise skipping one major meal daily to reduce calorie intake
Encourage gradual changes focusing on balanced meals and portion control
Eliminate all carbohydrates and fats from the diet

question: A 15-day-old male infant is brought to the pediatric outpatient department with poor feeding, excessive sleepiness, and persistent jaundice since birth. The mother reports that the baby rarely cries and has not regained his birth weight. On examination, the infant has a large anterior fontanelle, hypotonia, macroglossia, and an umbilical hernia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

43-year-old female presented with complaint of painless swelling in right side of the neck for 4 months, which is increasing in size. Her pulse is 104b/min, Blood pressure: 110/70mmHg, Afebrile. There is about 4x3 cm, firm, non-tender, swelling on left side of neck, which is moving on deglutition. What would be the most appropriate initial radiological investigation in this patient?

32 year old female came to your clinic with painless swelling left side of neck for 2 month. She has history of heat intolerance, palpitation and weight loss. Her pulse is 120b/min, BP: 140/80mmHg, her palms are moist and hands have fine tremors. There is about 3x4cm, soft, non-tender, swelling on left side of neck, overlying skin is normal, swelling is moving on deglutition. What would be the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old woman presents with complaints of fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, and constipation for 6 months. Her pulse is 60b/mins BP:110/60mmHg. Palms are dry. Neck examination is unremarkable. What is the most appropriate initial investigation in this patient?

A 55-year-old woman presents with severe lumbar pain and hematuria. She has history of recurrent renal stones. She also complaints of bone pains and constipation. Laboratory results show elevated serum calcium and raised PTH levels. What is the most appropriate initial management in this patient?

A neurosurgeon is looking at a MRI brain scan of a 50-year female showing a tumor growth that interrupts the vascular circulation between the hypothalamus and pituitary gland. Which vascular system is most likely affected that impacts hormone regulation?
During brain surgery, a structure lying just above the pituitary gland is carefully avoided by a neurosurgeon to prevent hormonal imbalance. Which structure is being referred to?

During a trans-sphenoidal surgical approach to the pituitary gland, the neurosurgeon must take special care to avoid damaging a structure situated superior to the pituitary that plays a central role in regulating pituitary hormone secretion. Which structure is most likely being referred to?
Strychnine poisoning primarily causes toxicity by:

answers.option: Blocking glycine-mediated inhibition in spinal cord

question: A characteristic feature that helps differentiate strychnine poisoning from tetanus is:
What is the most common cause of death in strychnine poisoning ?

answers.option: Respiratory failure due to muscle spasm

question: Which drug is used to reverse the enzyme inhibition caused by organophosphate poisoning?
Organophosphate compounds produce toxicity by:
The earliest and most sensitive clinical sign of organophosphate poisoning is:
Carbon monoxide poisoning causes tissue hypoxia mainly by which mechanism ?
A cherry-red discoloration of the skin in carbon monoxide poisoning is ?
The most effective treatment for severe carbon monoxide poisoning is ?
Dhatura poisoning produces its toxic effects due to ?

A 44-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus presents to her primary care physician for follow-up. She is currently being managed with an oral glucocorticoid agent. The most likely mechanism of action of this medication involves which of the following?

A 66-year-old woman with a history of Cushing's disease treated with oral glucocorticoids presents to her primary care physician for follow-up. She was recently hospitalized for a hip fracture following a fall. What is the most likely mechanism for hip fracture in this patient?

A 28-year-old man who is obese is found to have a hemoglobin A1c of 9.5%. He has been unable to adequately control his blood sugar with diet alone. His physician prescribe which of the following longest acting insulin to provide this patient a low, baseline insulin dose that will last throughout the day?

A 23-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with an enlarging neck mass and weight loss. The large mass is seen in the midline of the neck. She has lost 15 lb over the past month, feels like her heart is racing, and is always hot. The patient is diagnosed with Graves' disease and started on propylthiouracil. Which of the following is a side effect of propylthiouracil?

A young couple (25-year-old male, 23-year-old female) wants to start a family. They have not conceived after 1-year of unprotected intercourse. Infertility evaluation revealed no abnormalities in the female partner and low sperm count in the male. Which of the following is a drug that is purified from the urine of postmenopausal women and is used to promote spermatogenesis in infertile men?

A 29-year-old woman in her 41-week of gestation and has been in labor for 12-hours. Although her uterine contractions had been strong and regular initially, they had diminished in force during the past hour. Which of the following agents would be used to facilitate this woman's labor and delivery?

A 3-year-old girl presented with hirsutism, breast enlargement, and a height and bone age that was consistent with an age of 9. Diagnostic testing revealed precocious puberty. Which of the following is the most appropriate drug for treatment of this patient's precocious puberty?
The decision is made to treat hyperthyroidism patient with methimazole. Methimazole decreases serum concentrations of (T3) primarily by which of the following mechanism?

answers.option: Inhibiting the uptake of iodide by cells in the thyroid
Preventing the addition of iodine to tyrosine residues on thyroglobulin
Increasing the peripheral metabolism of T3

question: A 15-year boy with Type-1 Diabetes is brought to the hospital complaining of dizziness & lethargy. Laboratory findings include severe hyperglycemia, ketoacidosis and a blood pH of 7.15 (normal pH 7.35 - 7.45). Which of the following agent shall be administered to achieve rapid control of severe ketoacidosis?

A 32-year-old woman presents with progressive fatigue, unintentional weight loss, generalized weakness, salt craving, and dizziness on standing for the last two months. On examination, she has hyperpigmentation of the buccal mucosa, low blood pressure, and postural hypotension. What is the most appropriate initial investigation to confirm the suspected diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presents with progressive central obesity, facial rounding, acne, and increased facial hair over the past six months. She reports proximal muscle weakness and irregular menstrual cycles. On examination, she has purple abdominal striae, hypertension, and bruising. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial screening investigation for this patient?

A 26-year-old woman presents with amenorrhea, galactorrhea, and decreased libido for four months. She also complains of frequent headaches and blurred vision. On physical examination, bilateral peripheral visual field defects are noted. Which of the following investigations is most appropriate as an initial diagnostic test?

A 55-year-old woman presents with fatigue, constipation, bone pain, and recurrent renal stones over the last year. On examination, she has generalized muscle weakness. Laboratory evaluation shows mild hypercalcemia. Which of the following investigations is most appropriate to confirm the suspected diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man presents with vomiting, abdominal pain, and rapid breathing. He has a history of type 1 diabetes and missed insulin doses for two days. Examination shows dehydration. Laboratory findings reveal hyperglycemia and ketonemia. Which acid-base disturbance is most likely present?

answers.option: Metabolic acidosis with increased anion gap

question: A 50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes is evaluated during a routine follow-up visit. She is asymptomatic but is found to have persistent microalbuminuria on urine examination. Her blood pressure is 146/92 mmHg, and serum creatinine levels are within normal limits. She is not currently on antihypertensive therapy. Which drug is most appropriate to prevent progression of diabetic nephropathy?

A 22-year-old man with type 1 diabetes presents with sweating, tremors, palpitations, and confusion one hour after taking his usual insulin dose but missing breakfast. Symptoms improve rapidly after oral glucose administration. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presents with weight loss despite increased appetite, heat intolerance, palpitations, and anxiety for 4 months. Examination shows diffuse goiter, exophthalmos, fine tremors, and warm moist skin. Laboratory tests reveal suppressed TSH with elevated T3 and T4 levels. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man presented with polyuria and polydipsia for the past 4 months. On physical examination, there are no specific findings. Laboratory findings include serum Na+ 155 mmol/L (high); K+ 3.9 mmol/L, Cl- 111 mmol/L, CO2 27 mmol/L, glucose 84 mg/dL, creatinine 1 mg/dL. The specific gravity of urine is 1.002 (low). Which of the following hormone is most likely to be deficient in this patient?

A 35-year-old woman presented with complaints of feeling of fullness in her neck but has no other complaints. The enlargement has been gradual and painless for more than 1 year. Physical examination confirms diffuse enlargement of the thyroid gland without any apparent masses. Laboratory studies of thyroid function show a normal free T4 level and a slightly increased TSH level. What is the most likely cause of these findings?

A 40-year-old woman notices that her gloves from the previous winter no longer fit her hands. Her friends remark that her facial features have changed in the past year and that her voice seems deeper. On physical examination, she is afebrile. Her blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. She has coarse facial features. A radiograph of the foot shows an increased amount of soft tissue beneath the calcaneus. Which of the following statement is more appropriate for her condition?

A 40-year-old woman presents with increasing feeling of fullness in her neck for the past 7 months. On physical examination, her thyroid gland is enlarged and nodular. A fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the thyroid is done. She undergoes thyroidectomy. Gross examination of the thyroid shows a thyroid neoplasm; microscopically, the neoplasm is composed of spindle-shaped cells forming nests and trabeculae. There is a prominent pink hyaline stroma. Which of the following immune histochemical stains is most likely to be useful in the diagnosis of this neoplasm?

A 44-year-old man sees his physician because he felt a "lump" on the left side of his neck. Physical examination shows a nontender nodule on the left lobe of the thyroid gland. A cervical node is enlarged and nontender. Laboratory studies show no thyroid autoantibodies in his serum, and the T4 and TSH levels are normal. A thyroidectomy is performed; the figure shows the high-power microscopic appearance of the nodule. Which of the following is most likely to contribute to the development of the thyroid nodule in this patient?

A 62-year-old man has been concerned about a gradual weight gain over the past 30 years. He is 174 cm (5 ft 7 inches) tall and weighs 91 kg (BMI 30). He is taking no medications. On physical examination, he has decreased sensation to pinprick and light touch over the lower extremities. Patellar reflexes are reduced. Motor strength seems to be normal in all extremities. Laboratory studies show glucose of 269 mg/dL, creatinine of 1.9 mg/dL, total cholesterol of 220 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol of 27 mg/dL, and triglycerides of 261 mg/dL. A chest radiograph shows mild cardiomegaly. Five years later, he has claudication in the lower extremities when he exercises. Based on these findings, which of the following complications is most likely to occur in this patient?

A 27-year-old woman experienced sudden severe abdominal pain. On physical examination, she had marked abdominal tenderness and guarding. Laboratory studies showed serum glucose, 76 mg/dL; calcium, 12.2 mg/dL; and parathyroid hormone, 62 pg/mL (normal range 9 to 60 pg/mL). During surgery, four enlarged parathyroid glands were found and excised, with reimplantation of one half of one gland. After the surgery, her serum calcium concentration returned to normal. Three years later, she had an episode of upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Abdominal MRI indicated multiple 1-to-2 cm mass lesions in the pancreas. Two years later, she now has galactorrhea. Which of the following lesions is now most likely to be present?

answers.option: Small Cell Anaplastic Carcinoma of the lung

question: A 23-year-old, previously healthy woman died suddenly after complaining of a headache the previous day. At autopsy, her adrenal glands are enlarged, and there are extensive bilateral cortical hemorrhages. Which of the following organisms best accounts for these findings?

A survey is conducted on medical students' mental and emotional wellbeing. The questionnaire contains a "How you feel about life in medical college?" There are no options for the answer and each participant can freely write exactly how they feel. Which one of the following options is the most appropriate classification of the above question?

A survey was conducted to assess the opinion of students regarding internet service and free breakfast at the campus. It contained a "Should the administration provide high speed internet and free breakfast at the campus for all students?" Which one of the following options is the most appropriate classification of the above question?
In which of the following scenarios is surgery most clearly indicated for multinodular goiter?

answers.option: History of living in an iodine-deficient region
Patient concern regarding the cosmetic appearance of the neck
Presence of more than three nodules on ultrasound

question: A 52-year-old male with a significant smoking history presents with progressive proximal muscle weakness, facial puffiness ("moon facies"), and hyperpigmentation. Laboratory studies reveal significantly elevated serum cortisol and ACTH levels that are not suppressed by high-dose dexamethasone. Which of the following is the most likely underlying mechanism for his clinical presentation?

answers.option: Paraneoplastic secretion of PTHrP by Squamous Cell Carcinoma
Ectopic CRH production by a bronchial carcinoid tumor
Ectopic ACTH production by Small Cell Lung Carcinoma

question: A 48-year-old female with a history of prolonged glucocorticoid therapy for rheumatoid arthritis presents with fatigue, muscle weakness, and mild hypotension. Laboratory tests show low cortisol levels, low ACTH levels, and normal aldosterone levels. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

45-year-old patient presents with persistent hypertension and muscle weakness. Laboratory studies reveal hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis. Imaging identifies a solitary, well-circumscribed yellow mass on the left adrenal gland. Histopathological examination shows lipid-laden clear cells resembling those of the zona fasciculata. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is considered the gold standard diagnostic approach for confirming Growth hormone deficiency in children?

A 12-year-old patient presents with heat intolerance, progressive weight loss despite a good appetite, and increased anxiety. Physical examination reveals a fine resting tremor and a diffusely enlarged, non-tender thyroid gland. A radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) scan shows diffuse, increased uptake throughout the gland. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line medical treatment for this patient?

A 42-year-old female is found to have a 1.8cm firm, non-tender nodule in the right lobe of her thyroid during a routine physical exam. Laboratory studies show a normal TSH level. An ultrasound of the neck confirms the solid nodule and reveals microcalcifications and irregular borders. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?

A 52-year-old male is diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus during a routine screening. His Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) is 7.4%, and his fasting plasma glucose is 145 mg/dL. He has no history of cardiovascular or renal disease. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line management for this patient?
Which of the following metabolic disorders is caused by metformin?

A 45-year-old female with a history of gallstones presents to the emergency department with severe epigastric pain that radiates to her back, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Laboratory studies show significantly elevated serum amylase and lipase. Which of the following histological findings would be most characteristic of this condition?

A 34-year-old male with a long-standing history of Schizophrenia is charged with the attempted murder of his neighbor. During the trial, his legal team argues that at the time of the offense, the patient was experiencing a severe psychotic episode and truly did not understand the nature of his actions or that they were wrong. Which of the following legal standards is most likely being applied to determine if the defendant is "not guilty by reason of insanity"?

A 50-year-old male with a history of Ischemic Heart Disease, Hypertension, and Type 2 Diabetes underwent Coronary Artery Bypass Graft surgery one year ago. His current medications include oral hypoglycemics, anti-hypertensives, and Amiodarone for arrhythmia management. He now presents with symptoms of fatigue and cold intolerance. Laboratory studies show: TSH: Increased, Free T3 and T4: Decreased. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his thyroid status?

A 35-year-old female presents with symptoms of hyperthyroidism, including palpitations, weight loss, and heat intolerance. On physical examination, several findings are noted. Which of the following signs is considered most specific for Graves' Disease?

Question:
A 62-year-old male with persistent Atrial Fibrillation is being treated with Amiodarone. During a follow-up visit, he reports new-onset fatigue and weight gain. Laboratory studies confirm primary hypothyroidism (Elevated TSH, Low Free T4). His underlying arrhythmia is currently well-controlled on his current dose of Amiodarone. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

answers.option: Decrease the dosage of Amiodarone by 50%
Continue Amiodarone and initiate Levothyroxine therapy

question: A clinical researcher is conducting a study on the prevalence of hypertension in patients visiting the Outpatient Department (OPD). The researcher uses a computer program to generate a list of random medical record numbers from all patients registered in the hospital’s electronic database for that day. Each selected patient is then approached for the study. Which of the following sampling methods is being utilized?

A hospital administrator is conducting a patient satisfaction survey. They obtain a list of all patients discharged in the last month and decide to select every 10th person on the list, starting from a randomly chosen point. Which of the following sampling techniques is being employed?

A 38-year-old patient currently undergoing Anti-Tuberculous Therapy (ATT) for pulmonary tuberculosis presents with progressive fatigue, nausea, and recent episodes of lightheadedness. Laboratory studies reveal hyponatremia and hyperkalemia. Given the high association between disseminated tuberculosis and adrenal involvement, which of the following is the best initial test to confirm a diagnosis of primary adrenal insufficiency?
Which of the following drugs increases calcium sensitivity on the PTH receptor to reduce PTH secretion?

A 28-year-old male is brought to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident resulting in a traumatic brain injury. On the second day of admission, the nursing staff notes a sudden increase in urine output. Laboratory studies show: Serum Sodium: 152mEq/L (High), Serum Osmolality: 310mOsm/kg (High), Urine Osmolality: 110mOsm/kg (Low). A water deprivation test is performed, and the urine osmolality remains low. Which of the following is the best long-term treatment for this patient’s condition?

A 29-year-old female with Graves' disease presents with significant heat intolerance, persistent sweating, and skin that feels warm and moist to the touch. Which of the following best explains the primary physiological mechanism responsible for these specific findings?

answers.option: Decreased sweat gland sensitivity to acetylcholine
Selective activation of alpha-1 adrenergic receptors
Increased Basal Metabolic Rate and Sympathetic Overactivity

question: A research team is planning a large-scale randomized controlled trial to evaluate a new surgical intervention. Before launching the full study, they conduct a small-scale version of the project on a limited number of participants to check the validity of the study. What is this process called?

A 4-year-old child is brought to the emergency department by his mother, who appears pale and fatigued. On examination, he has mild jaundice, and his urine is notably dark brown (cola-colored). Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's presentation?

A 32-year-old male presents with a painless, slow-growing mass in the midline of his neck, just below the hyoid bone. On physical examination, the clinician observes that the mass ascends when the patient swallows (deglutition) and also elevates when the patient protrudes his tongue. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old female presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of blurred vision, double vision (diplopia), and difficulty swallowing (dysphagia). She notes that the symptoms began shortly after she consumed home-canned green beans. Which of the following is the most likely causative agent?

A 34-year-old male with Graves' disease was started on Methimazole, but the medication was discontinued after he developed severe agranulocytosis. He has a history of significant Graves' ophthalmopathy and refuses radioactive iodine (RAI) therapy due to concerns about worsening his eye disease. He is now being evaluated for surgical intervention to achieve definitive control of his hyperthyroidism. Which of the following is the best surgical procedure for this patient?

A 45-year-old male with clinical features of acromegaly undergoes transsphenoidal resection of a pituitary macroadenoma. Histopathological examination using electron microscopy reveals the presence of distinct, pale, perinuclear inclusion bodies within the tumor cells. Immunohistochemical staining confirms these inclusions are composed of cytokeratin filaments. Which of the following is the most likely pathological finding?

A newborn infant is noted to have ambiguous genitalia (virilization) at birth. Within the second week of life, the infant develops vomiting, poor feeding, and severe dehydration. Laboratory results show Hyponatremia, Hyperkalemia, and Metabolic Acidosis. Which enzyme deficiency is most likely responsible for this "salt-wasting" presentation?

A 58-year-old patient with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus is started on a new oral hypoglycemic agent to improve postprandial glucose control. Two months later, the patient presents to the emergency department with severe, constant epigastric pain radiating to the back, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Laboratory tests show a serum lipase level three times the upper limit of normal. Which of the following medications is most likely responsible for this presentation?
Which diabetic drug causes bone fractures as a side effect?

A 12-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrician by her parents due to a noticeable change in her school performance over the last two terms; her grades have declined, and her teachers report she seems "sluggish." The parents also note she has struggled with persistent constipation for 6 months and has gained 5 kg despite no change in her diet. On examination, her heart rate is 60 bpm (bradycardia) and she has a palpable, non-tender enlargement of the thyroid gland. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old male from an endemic region presents with chronic fatigue, weight loss, and hyperpigmentation of the skin and palmar creases. Laboratory studies confirm primary adrenal insufficiency. A CT scan of the abdomen shows bilateral enlargement of the adrenal glands with areas of calcification. A fine-needle aspiration is performed, and the pathology report notes the presence of caseating granulomas and acid-fast bacilli. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's adrenal failure?

A 40-year-old female presents with chronic fatigue, orthostatic hypotension, and new-onset hyperpigmentation. Laboratory testing confirms low morning cortisol and elevated ACTH. A CT scan of the abdomen reveals bilaterally shrunken (atrophic) adrenal glands. A biopsy of the gland would most likely show a diffuse lymphocytic infiltration and loss of cortical cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Prolactin-producing pituitary adenoma is associated with which of the following genes?

A 55-year-old female undergoes a thyroid lobectomy for a solitary, 3cm cold nodule.  Two years later, she presents to the emergency department with severe hip pain after a minor trip. Radiographs reveal a pathological fracture of the femoral neck with a clear "punched-out" osteolytic lesion. A biopsy of the bone lesion shows well-differentiated follicles containing colloid. Which of the following is the most likely primary diagnosis?
Which of the following syndromes is most commonly associated with both congenital and acquired autoimmune hypothyroidism?

A 55-year-old male presents with generalized body aches, fatigue, and persistent hypertension. Laboratory evaluation reveals: Hemoglobin (Hb): 10g/dL, (Anemia) Calcium: 11.8mg/dl (High), Albumin: 4.9g/dL (Normal/High-normal), Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP): 230U/L (High), Parathyroid Hormone (PTH): Markedly elevated, Creatinine: 1.1mg/dL (Normal). 
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old male is brought to the emergency department after a camping trip. His friends report that he ingested part of a wild plant on a dare. He is currently agitated and confused. Physical examination reveals: flushed, hot, and dry skin; mydriasis; dry mucous membranes; and tachycardia. Which of the following plants did he most likely ingest?

A 45-year-old female is diagnosed with an adrenal cortical adenoma after presenting with signs of Cushing syndrome. Genetic analysis of the tumor tissue reveals a mutation in the CTNNB1 gene. Which of the following best describes the molecular consequence of this mutation?

answers.option: Decrease in cAMP signaling in the adrenal cortex
Decreased expression of the glucocorticoid receptor
Inactivation of the protein kinase A regulatory subunit
Loss-of-function of the TP53 tumor suppressor

question: Which of the following is primarily responsible for the direct destruction of thyroid follicular cells in Hashimoto thyroiditis?

A 38-year-old female presents with persistent fatigue, weight loss, and recurrent episodes of dizziness. On physical examination, she has low blood pressure and increased pigmentation in her skin creases and oral mucosa. Laboratory studies reveal Hyponatremia and Hyperkalemia. An abdominal CT scan shows bilaterally atrophied (shrunken) adrenal glands. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old female presents to the emergency department with sudden, severe epigastric pain that radiates to her back. She is obese and reports a history of intermittent right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals. Laboratory results show a significantly elevated serum lipase and elevated direct bilirubin. An ultrasound confirms the presence of multiple small gallstones. What is the most likely pathological mechanism for her current presentation?

answers.option: Stone obstructing the common bile duct

question: A 32-year-old female with Graves' disease presents with a "staring" expression. On physical examination, the upper limbus of the sclera is visible when she looks straight ahead (lid retraction), and there is a noticeable delay of the upper eyelid as she looks downward (lid lag). Which of the following is the primary physiological cause of the lid retraction and visualization of the upper sclera in this patient?

answers.option: Deposition of GAGs in the extraocular muscles
Fibrosis of the levator palpebrae superioris

question: A 55-year-old male with a 15-year history of poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus presents for a routine eye exam. Fundoscopy reveals multiple dot-and-blot hemorrhages, microaneurysms, and hard exudates. Which of the following is involved in the pathogenesis of this mechanism?

answers.option: Proliferation of the internal limiting membrane
Accumulation of sorbitol within retinal pericytes
Reduced sorbitol production in the retina

question: A patient is brought to the emergency department with severe Dhatura poisoning. Which of the following is the specific pharmacological antidote used to reverse anti-cholinergic effects?
